title: El mandado
goal: Send a kid on an errand and get the change back
culture: Sending a chavalo to the pulpería is completely normal and he expects a few córdobas for going. This is also the first person in Granada you address as VOS instead of usted: a child, and later a friend. Getting that switch right is most of sounding Nicaraguan.

beats.es: ¿Le hago mandado, señor? Ando en la bici.
beats.objective: Ask him to run an errand
beats.en: Would you run an errand for me?
beats.good: Un mandado is an errand and the whole arrangement is in the word. He will already know which pulpería.

beats.en: Here you go. A hundred córdobas.
beats.good: Aquí está hands something over. Pesos in the street, córdobas on the note, and everybody says pesos.
El vuelto is the change. Say it lightly and it is not an accusation — it is the arrangement, and it is why he gets tipped rather than skimming.

beats.es: Aquí está todo, señor. Conté bien.
beats.good: Para VOS, not para usted. He is a child, so he gets vos — and this is the first time in the whole game you use it. Getting that switch right matters more than any verb ending you will study.
